See also: militaré and militäre

Asturian

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

militare

  1. inflection of militar:
    1. first/third-person singular pluperfect indicative
    2. first/third-person singular imperfect preterite subjunctive

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /mi.liˈta.re/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -are
  • Hyphenation: mi‧li‧tà‧re

Etymology 1

[edit]

Probably borrowed from Latin mīlitāris.

Adjective

[edit]

militare m or f by sense (plural militari)

  1. military
  2. army
Derived terms
[edit]
  • militarismo
  • militarista
  • militarmente
  • premilitare (“premilitary”)

Noun

[edit]

militare m (plural militari)

  1. serviceman

Etymology 2

[edit]

From Latin mīlitāre.

Verb

[edit]

militàre (first-person singular present mìlito, first-person singular past historic militài, past participle militàto, auxiliary avére) (intransitive)

  1. to serve as a soldier, to militate
  2. (figurative) to fight [with a ‘for (an idea)’]
  3. to participate actively (in a political party or organization)
  4. to militate [with a favore di ‘in favor of (an argument or fact)’]
